stem.en: A student says: "The pyramid was a completely new idea with nothing before it." What does the book show?

text.en: The student is right: pyramids had no earlier form.

feedback.en: The book says otherwise: mastabas came first, and they were placed one on top of the other to form a pyramid.

text.en: Pyramids came first, and mastabas were later, cheaper copies.

feedback.en: This is the wrong way round. The mastaba came first.

text.en: Pyramids were copied from Sumerian ziggurats.

feedback.en: Both are stepped, but a ziggurat was a temple and a pyramid was a tomb. The book links the pyramid to the mastaba.

text.en: Pyramids grew out of mastabas placed one on top of the other.

explanation.en: A mastaba was a rectangular structure over a burial chamber. Gradually mastabas were stacked to form a pyramid, as at Saqqara.

hints.en: What was placed over a burial chamber before there were pyramids?
